rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to assess whether combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses pca_n2000 (RNA) and resnet50 (image) with simple concatenation fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration by testing a key design choice (multimodal vs. single-modality) while using standard encoders to minimize complexity, providing a foundation for future comparisons.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (concat fusion) achieved 0.526592 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of changing the fusion method to 'weighted' while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether weighted fusion improves performance compared to concat, a critical design choice in multimodal models.

The existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 have ~0.52 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (a key design choice) with avgpool aggregation (a potential performance booster) while keeping fusion as concat (similar to previous best). It isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, which are critical factors with sparse evidence, and balances exploration of multiprofile with minimal changes to other parameters.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve high accuracy (0.618). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method to weighted (config_019) further improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. This balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile setup with exploration of critical design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with a more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder and switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer, while retaining weighted fusion. This isolates the effect of the image encoder and aggregation method, which are critical design choices with potential for performance gains. It balances exploitation of the successful multimodal/multiprofile direction with exploration of stronger components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) in the same setup improves performance. It isolates the impact of the image encoder while keeping other parameters consistent, addressing uncertainty about whether newer encoders could further boost accuracy. This is a high-impact comparison given the strong prior performance of the base configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.638999). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex encoder) could further improve performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. This is a critical design choice with potential for high reward, and it aligns with the principle of balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_031: 0.6776). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) and aggregation method (avgpool → transformer) to explore if combining a more powerful image encoder with transformer-based aggregation further improves performance. This clarifies the impact of these design choices on accuracy, prioritizing exploitation of the promising scvi_n200 RNA encoder while exploring potential gains from advanced image processing.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and transformer aggregation/weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a newer RNA encoder) in the same high-performing architecture could further improve accuracy. It directly isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while maintaining other successful components, balancing exploitation of proven elements with exploration of a novel encoder.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_031: 0.6776). This experiment tests the effect of fusion method (concat vs. weighted) on performance using the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation. It clarifies whether the fusion strategy significantly impacts accuracy, which is critical for optimizing the model.
